_doc: The Guide's glossary (T-2662, design doc section 03 'Locked terms', NAV-804). One row per locked term, in the order section 03 lists them; `meaning` is what a visitor reads on tap and in the Guide, at most 15 words. `rests_on` names the files in this repository that make the meaning true, and is data, never shown. Gated by tools/check_guide.py.

terms.meaning: A source says so, and we name it.
terms.note: Section 03 drafts 'A source from the time says so.' Not used: an Attested fact here can rest on later scholarship (a 1963 survey, a museum's own pages), and AGENTS.md defines the grade as 'a source states it. Cite the source.'

terms.meaning: Worked out from clues about this exact thing.
terms.note: Section 03's line, with 'place' widened to 'thing': AGENTS.md says 'reasoned from evidence about this particular thing', and the grade is given to people and attributes as well as places.

terms.meaning: No record exists. We built it so the street makes sense, and say so.
Recolor the world by grade, or hide a grade completely.
terms.note: Section 03's line as written; confidence.js tints by grade and hides a grade (`setHidden`).

terms.meaning: Our list of the choices we made without a source, and why.
terms.note: Section 03 drafts 'Every choice we made without a source, listed by name.' Not used: the list has 608 entries, many covering a whole class of choices (one entry for hundreds of roofs), so it is not one row per choice. Each entry gives the decision and why.

terms.meaning: Where our facts come from: books, maps, photos, newspapers and more, each one named.
terms.note: Section 03 lists 'maps, photos, letters, newspapers'. The records are mostly websites and books, with photographs, maps, newspapers and seven manuscripts; 'and more' keeps the line true without a list.

terms.meaning: Short guided walks through the town, stop by stop.
terms.note: Section 03 gives no line. A jaunt is a walk with a premise, an opening and stops (data/jaunts/, 1835 and 1904).
